Background concepts / WEBFRONT

React components and state

Describing a component, updating its state and integrating it with C++.

Notation conventions

Function names, types, commands, options and filenames appear in monospace, for example describe, wf test or main.cpp. Italics introduce a term at its definition. Code blocks give the fragments to enter; the preceding text states their location and prerequisites.

Describing a component ↓Updating state ↓Receiving an asynchronous reply ↓The WebFront adapter ↓

Describing a component

A React component describes part of an interface from its properties and state. JSX resembles HTML but belongs to the JavaScript or TypeScript programme.

When state changes, React recalculates the component description and applies the necessary DOM updates. The rendering function should therefore describe the presentation corresponding to the current state.

Updating state

This fragment belongs inside a function component and assumes useState has been imported from React. The function g => g + 1 calculates a new value from the previous one.

To update a grid held in state, create a new value and pass it to the setter. Mutating the existing array does not correctly describe the change to React.

SOURCE
const [generation, setGeneration] = useState(0);
<button onClick={() => setGeneration(g => g + 1)}>
    {generation}
</button>

Receiving an asynchronous reply

A C++ call may finish after a reset or after the requesting component has unmounted. Before updating state following an await, check that the reply still belongs to the current session.

Subscriptions created in useEffect require a clean-up function. The Life starter illustrates both obligations.

The WebFront adapter

The optional @webfront/react package provides createStore, useStore and Island. It is distributed separately from React and WebFront’s core resources. examples/life/react combines a React interface with a panel built in C++.

Unmounting requires coordinated release: React must wait until the C++ owner has completed its clean-up before removing the island. The React guide describes this protocol.
